aggregate_initial_judgment: Read before opening seat totals. Claim: GPT-4o + Molmo-7B extract target/obstacle pixels from one aerial image + text, map them to world coordinates with a planar camera-height/FoV formula, and an onboard point-to-point NMPC with an obstacle penalty flies the mission; 33.75% faster than an off-the-shelf autopilot and 54.6% faster than a human pilot. Evidence: two arena layouts, one instruction, one timed flight per condition (Table III), Vicon check of perception only (Tables I-II). Exp1 vs Exp2 share the multimodal targets, so they isolate the controller, but the autopilot is unidentified and n=1; the human arm has a different timing start. No success/arrival or collision criterion, no repeats, no holdout statement. In scope only on the broad reading (frontier LLM/VLM + perception + controller driving a UAV, open loop, no verification/hand-back). Expected: descriptive arena result, offline evidence level, weak E.

paper.title: UAV-VLRR: Vision-Language Informed NMPC for Rapid Response in UAV Search and Rescue
paper.central_claim: Integrating vision-language mission interpretation with onboard point-to-point obstacle-avoiding NMPC enables faster and safe UAV search-and-rescue response, averaging 33.75% faster than an off-the-shelf autopilot and 54.6% faster than a human pilot.
paper.scope_note: In scope on the broad reading: a frontier LLM (GPT-4o) plus a VLM drive a UAV through perception and an NMPC controller. Open-loop one-shot pipeline without verification or hand-back; son55's edge-scope flag recorded, no out_of_scope precedent applies (frontier model present).

M.reason: son55 adopted (sol 3). Division of labour and the 'no tracking constraint tolerates model mismatch' rationale are a real mechanism, but the load-bearing planar height/FoV assumption is weak and the data already show its bias (21/24 coordinates shrink, agg:A03); no distinguishing prediction for the VLM side.
